method: Viewed all 27 corrected PNG files at original detail using view_image. Rail and road/roof atlases compare requested 0/1/4/8 second frames; full views show requested 0 and/or 4 seconds.
observations: At desktop-wide, compact and landscape, rail atlases show blue and orange trains moving between sampled frames and passing behind poles; no obvious pole seams or missing train sections were observed in those captures.

Road/roof atlases show the cat changing position and pose on the rooftop; sampled residential windows change brightness. Full views preserve the skyline and visible rooftop support without the rejected horizontal floor stripe.
Wide 1920 and 3200 captures show moving trains, cat and cloud between the two frames, with image edges filled.
Extreme 2000x500 fills the frame and shows one moon, but side-extension mirroring visibly repeats chairs and rooftop structures; this is an accepted limitation of this extreme aspect ratio.
limitations: Finite still frames do not establish smoothness for all times, every cat pose or the full car route; star and distant window animation need separate local/time evidence.

Estimated best train RGB patch shifts at 0 to 1 requested second were 77, 46 and 60 physical pixels for desktop-wide, compact and landscape respectively. They are matching estimates, not exact speed measurements: frame timing and occlusion affect them.
These screenshots show the current generated image after correction, not a new generated artwork.
